Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the RenewaTech Global Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, please press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss RenewaTech Global's results for the Q2 2024. Joining me on today's call are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; David Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Maria Lopez, Chief Development Officer; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; and Tom Reilly, Chief Sustainability Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements. We encourage you to review the disclaimer in our press release and on our website regarding these statements.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong Q2 performance, driven by our continued focus on innovation, operational excellence, and sustainability. We are seeing strong demand for our renewable energy solutions across all markets.

As we execute on our mission to accelerate the global energy transition, let me share six key highlights from the quarter that underscore our leadership in utility-scale solar PV, onshore and offshore wind, battery energy storage systems, and emerging long-duration energy storage solutions.

First, our development pipeline additions and project milestones reflect another robust period of growth. We added 4.2 GW to our global development pipeline during Q2, bringing the total secured pipeline to 28.5 GW across 15 countries—a 17% increase quarter-over-quarter and 45% year-over-year. This stems from our disciplined origination strategy, using proprietary land acquisition tools, AI-driven site selection algorithms, and partnerships with landowners and utilities. By technology, solar PV saw 2.1 GW added, including the 800 MW SunForge portfolio in Arizona with TOPCon modules at 23.5% efficiency, optimized for high-irradiance, and the 500 MW Outback Solar Hub in New South Wales co-located with 200 MWh BESS pilots. These leverage declining module costs down 12% year-over-year per IRENA data and U.S. Inflation Reduction Act benefits like the 30% ITC plus domestic content adders, aiming for unlevered IRRs over 12%. Wind additions totaled 1.2 GW, blending onshore like the 600 MW Prairie Winds in Texas with GE Vernova 5.X-158 turbines and 15% projected capacity factors via wake steering software, and offshore such as the 400 MW Nordic Breeze floating project in Norway's North Sea partnering with Equinor on Volturnus TLP platforms, tapping REPowerEU targets with €100+/MWh auction premiums. Storage and hybrids added 900 MW/3.8 GWh, highlighted by the 500 MWh IronFlow iron-air LDES in California using Form Energy tech for 100-hour discharge at $20/kWh LCOE to address CAISO duck curve issues; hybrids now make up 35% of additions, up from 22% last year. Regionally, North America drove 55% or 2.3 GW via IRA PPAs from PG&E and ERCOT, Europe 25% or 1.05 GW amid German TSO reforms and UK CfD Round 5, APAC 15% or 630 MW from India SECI and Australian NEM where our solar-plus-storage LCOE undercuts coal by 25%, and Brazil the rest with 150 MW hydro-plus-solar. We achieved 18 key milestones, advancing 3.2 GW to shovel-ready, supporting FY24 guidance of 5-7 GW to NTP. Permitting successes included Army Corps 404 for 1.1 GW U.S. solar, with queue times at 18 months versus industry 36 months per LBNL; Europe grid agreements for 800 MW Dutch wind under TEN-E. PPAs signed totaled 12 GWh, like the 15-year 400 MW with Google for Silicon Valley Solar + Megapack at $25/MWh all-in and 95% availability. FIDs hit on 1.2 GW unlocking $2.8B EPC with Bechtel and Fluor; construction started on 900 MW including Empire Wind 300 MW offshore, Texas Plains 400 MW onshore, and SunRiver 200 MW solar-plus-4 GWh BESS, with EPC at $850/kW. CODs delivered 450 MW, like Horizon BESS 250 MW/1 GWh in PJM at 98.5% uptime and $150/kW ancillaries, beating Fluence peers. Shovel-ready grew 22% to 12 GW with 4 GW 2025 CODs targeted at 10-12% IRRs, aided by $1.2B tax equity with US Bancorp and Goldman Sachs, module deflation to $0.22/Wp, BESS to $140/kWh, 80% hedged commodities, and digital twins for 15% O&M savings. Q3 will see 2 GW more, including green hydrogen pilots with ITM Power electrolyzers for the $100B H2 market per BloombergNEF, driving 25% EBITDA CAGR to 2027.

Second, capital recycling through asset sale transactions continues as a core value-creation lever in our developer-owner-operator model. We avoid holding stabilized assets long-term, instead recycling proceeds into high-return greenfield development for optimal balance sheet and risk-adjusted shareholder returns, akin to NextEra and Ørsted. In Q2, we closed two deals for $1.2B gross proceeds, lifting trailing 12-month volume to $3.8B, up 45% YoY and funding 25% of year-to-date capex for our 15 GW pipeline—now 28.5 GW. Headline sales: 450 MW U.S. Southwest solar portfolio including King Solar and Desert Bloom in Arizona/California to Brookfield Renewable Partners and a European pension fund at 14x EBITDA multiple, 12.5% IRR, 2.3x equity multiple post-24 months P90 performance under PPAs with Southern California Edison and APS, enhanced by IRA 45Q and ITC transferability. Also, 300 MW Midwest onshore wind like Prairie Winds in Iowa/Illinois to BlackRock infra fund for $350M at 13x EBITDA, 11.8% IRR using Vestas V150s at 30% capacity factors and curtailment algorithms under MidAmerican PPAs. U.S. drove 70% or $2.7B TTM, supercharged by IRA for 18-24 month cycles; Europe 20% or $760M via 200 MW Spanish solar to Repsol at €45/MWh; APAC 10% with $380M Australian 250 MW Queensland solar to Macquarie at 15x EBITDA amid NEM spot rises. Proceeds cut net debt/EBITDA to 3.6x from 4.2x, boosted liquidity to $4.5B including $1.2B revolvers; 85% recycled to $2.5B in 5 GW construction at 15-18% IRRs, rest to repurchases at $42/share for 12% book accretion. Held assets average 4 years post-COD, 14-year contracts, 98% contracted; cumulative 8 GW divested since 2021 at 13.5x EBITDA, 12.2% IRR, outpacing S&P Clean Energy Index by 300 bps. This de-risks for ERCOT BESS at $250/kW-year ancillaries or Chile 500 MW H2 at $1.8/kg with $25/MWh solar; tailwinds include $500B global capex per BNEF, module costs down 15% YoY, $150B infra funds chasing 7-9% yields. Q3 queues $5-7B including 2 GW U.S. clusters and 400 MW offshore to Equinor, mitigating basis/permit risks with 20 GW buffer, 95% hedges for 20%+ EPS CAGR.

Third, capacity factor performance by technology drove margin expansion and cash flow. Company-wide blended FY23 was 34.2%, up 210 bps YoY, beating NREL by 300 bps via optimization, management, and siting. Solar PV on 12.5 GWdc (45% portfolio) hit 28.5% Q2, 27.8% FY, up from 26.2%; bifacial LONGi/Trina on 65% new with Nextracker boosted 8-12%; U.S. Southwest 7.2 GW like 800 MW Gemini Nevada at 32.1% with 2,300 kWh/m² GHI, robotic cleaning; Northeast C&I 18.4% improving via Oxford PV perovskites at 35%+; Australia 1.8 GW 29.2%, Europe 500 MW 24.7% gaining; target 30%+ by 2025 with 1.4:1 oversizing, GE Vernova AI soiling, repowering. Wind 15.3 GW (70/30 onshore/offshore) at 41.2% blended, up 180 bps over IRENA 35%; onshore 38.4% via 2.2 GW V150 repowers, Thunder Ranch Oklahoma 42.8% at 8.5 m/s; offshore 4.6 GW 52.1% like Vineyard Wind, German dips to 48%; U.S. 39.7%, hybrids lift 5-7%; $1.2B CapEx for 15 MW GE Haliade-X floating to 55%+. Storage 8.2 GWh LFP like Megapacks at 87.3% utilization, 92.1% RTE, 76.5% equivalent CF; FTM Gemini 1.2 GWh 89%, C&I 62%; low 1.8% degradation, Stem Athena AI 15% more cycles; CAISO 91%, Texas winter spreads; Australia pilots 85% RTE 100-hour. Hybrids target 50%+ like SunWindForge; $500M long-duration, Climeon forecasting for 15% gains, IRA/EU tailwinds support FY24 $4.2-4.5B EBITDA.

Fourth, our strategic priorities and outlook position us strongly amid LCOE drops making solar/wind competitive with gas and AI data center demand. Priorities: scale utility EPC/IPP with Q4 800 MW Gemini Nevada hybrid COD under 20-year NV Energy PPA at 12.5% IRR using TOPCon, 2.5 GW FY25 U.S. hybrids on IRA tax equity $1.2B, U.S. 45% growth post-FERC 2023; advance BESS like VerdantFlow 95% RTE, 1.2 GWh contracts including 500 MWh SCE, $250M R&D QuantumScape/Form Energy for hyperscaler 24/7 CF; expand EMEA/APAC with UK 500 MW wind at £44/MWh CfD, Australia 300 MW, India SECI under ₹2/kWh, 60% non-China supply; Nexus digital twins/NVIDIA for 18-20% EPC margins, drone O&M 99.5%, blockchain RECs. Q4 revenue $460-480M +28-33%, EBITDA 27-29%, FY24 $1.75B +35%, $450M FCF, $0.25/share dividend, $300M buybacks. FY25 $2.1-2.3B +30-35%, 3.2 GW CODs, $6.5B backlog, $580-620M EBITDA 28%, EPS $2.45-2.65; assumes $0.22/Wp modules, 85% tax credits. Risks: supply 2-3% margins, rates delay 500 MW, policy; 18-month visibility, 4x book-to-bill resilient in $1.7T market per BNEF.

Fifth, new PPAs secured totaled 850 MW across three utility-scale deals, growing backlog to 4.2 GW, up 28% QoQ for 2025 starts. ERCOT 300 MW solar-plus-200 MWh/4-hour BESS with hyperscaler like Google at 15-year $28/MWh levelized, 15% hybrid premium for 24/7 RE100, >28% P50 CF TOPCon. PJM 400 MW onshore wind with utility like Duke at 20-year $26/MWh GE 6.0 MW, CPI+1% escalators. Romania 150 MW floating solar Danube with industrial like ArcelorMittal at €32/MWh ($35 USD) 12-year, 18% CF Ocean Sun. Blended average $27.50/MWh, +9% QoQ, +18% YoY, reversing prior dips; IRA de-risking, polysilicon $8/kg, hyperscaler 12 GW YTD per LevelTen, REPowerEU €40-50/MWh. U.S. ERCOT $25-30 hybrids, PJM $24-28 wind, CAISO $22; Australia AUD55 ($37), India $30. PPA pipeline 12 GW including 2 GW hybrids for Q4 1 GW+ at >$28/MWh on 20% BESS cost drops; 17-year average life, 85% IG, value-add clauses for 12-14% IRRs, funds $2.5B revolver, 15% dividend hike.

Sixth, tax equity and project-level financing scaled our 5.2 GW portfolio post-IRA. Tax equity monetizes ITC/PTC via flips with banks/insurers at 40-60% capex for 6-8% IRR priority then sponsor control. Q2 $1.2B closed on 450 MW Desert Bloom solar, 300 MW Gulf Coast Wind II, 200 MW/800 MWh Horizon hybrid; JPM/US Bancorp $750M at 55% ITC with IRA adders for $850M equity relief. Southwest/ERCOT hybrids stack SGIP, Midwest PTC insurers; transferability adds tech buyers like Google, IRRs 7.2%. Project debt non-recourse 50-65% construction to 20-year term SOFR+125-175 bps on PPAs/DOE. Q2 $2.8B: $1.1B Desert Bloom green bond 4.85%, $650M Gulf Coast MUFG/KeyBanc $35/MWh PPA, $400M DOE LPO Horizon LFP for duck curve $120/kW ancillaries. Stack: tax 45-55%, debt 50-60%, sponsor 10-15% for <5.5% capital cost, 12.4% ROIC. Trends: spreads 200 bps, EU green bonds; risks hedged EPC, FERC queues. FY24 $4-5B targets 1.2 GW CODs, 10 GWh storage in $110B IRA capex.

These highlights position us exceptionally well. Now, I will turn the call over to David Chen to discuss our financial results in more detail.

David Chen:
Thank you, Sarah. We are very pleased with our financial performance in Q2. Revenue was $450 million, a 35% increase year-over-year. This increase was driven by higher project commissioning and energy sales. Gross margin was 28%, reflecting improved cost management and favorable pricing. Operating expenses were $130 million, primarily due to increased investments in R&D and sales and marketing. Net income was $90 million, or $0.82 per share. We ended the quarter with $1.5 billion in cash and cash equivalents. We are reaffirming our full-year guidance for revenue of $1.75 billion and earnings per share of $2.45 to $2.65.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Maria Lopez for an update on our project pipeline.

Maria Lopez:
Thank you, David. Our project pipeline continues to grow, with 28.5 GW of projects under development. We are making good progress on securing land rights, obtaining permits, and negotiating power purchase agreements, as detailed earlier. We expect to bring several new projects online in the coming quarters, including 2 GW more additions in Q3 with green hydrogen pilots. We are also actively exploring opportunities to expand our project portfolio through strategic acquisitions and partnerships.

Next, Dr. Vasquez will provide an update on our technology initiatives.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Maria. We are committed to developing and deploying innovative technologies that improve the efficiency and reliability of renewable energy systems. We are making significant progress on our research and development efforts, including advanced solar panel technologies like TOPCon bifacial and perovskite tandems, energy storage solutions such as IronFlow LDES iron-air systems for 100-hour dispatch, and smart grid technologies with AI EMS and digital twins. The development of IronFlow is expected to have revolutionary impacts on our future projects by achieving $20/kWh LCOE and enhancing grid resiliency. We believe that these technologies will play a critical role in accelerating the transition to a clean energy future.

And now, Tom Reilly will provide an update on our sustainability efforts.

Tom Reilly:
Thank you, Dr. Vasquez. We are committed to operating our business in a sustainable manner and minimizing our environmental impact. We have set ambitious goals for reducing our carbon emissions by 50% by 2030, improving our energy efficiency through advanced O&M, and promoting responsible resource management across our global footprint. We are also actively involved in community engagement and supporting local initiatives that promote sustainability, such as workforce training in host communities and biodiversity offsets. We believe that sustainability is not only the right thing to do but also makes good business sense, driving premium PPAs and investor demand.

I'll now turn the call back to Sarah for closing remarks.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Tom. In closing, we are confident that RenewaTech Global is well-positioned to capitalize on the growing demand for renewable energy. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering long-term value for our shareholders.

Operator, let's open the line for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, if you would like to register for a question, please press star then one on your touchtone phone. Our first question comes from John Mayer with GreenCapital Partners. Please go ahead.

John Mayer:
Can you provide more details on the regulatory environment for renewable energy projects in your key markets?

Sarah Thompson:
Thanks for the question, John. The regulatory landscape remains supportive overall, particularly with the IRA in the U.S. driving ITC/PTC extensions and adders that we've fully leveraged in our 2.3 GW North America additions. We've navigated FERC queue reforms effectively, reducing our wait times to 18 months versus the industry 36 months, as seen in our Army Corps 404 permits for 1.1 GW solar and BOEM approvals for Empire Wind. In Europe, REPowerEU and TEN-E have accelerated offshore like our Dutch 800 MW grid agreements and UK CfD auctions. APAC benefits from NEM reforms and SECI tenders, though we monitor Brazil permitting. Our early interconnection filings and 20 GW buffer keep us ahead.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with EcoInvest Advisors. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen:
How is the company addressing the challenges of energy storage integration with your renewable energy projects?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Great question, Lisa. Storage integration is central to our hybrids, now 35% of pipeline. We've deployed 8.2 GWh with 92.1% RTE and 87.3% utilization, using LFP Megapack equivalents and IronFlow LDES for 100-hour at Gemini 1.2 GWh capturing 95% curtailments. AI like Stem Athena optimizes cycles in CAISO/ERCOT for $120-250/kW-year ancillaries, while DC-block architectures hit 98.5% uptime. Partnerships with Form Energy and QuantumScape target solid-state 800 Wh/kg, smoothing intermittency for 50%+ effective CFs in SunWindForge, ahead of duck curve and data center needs.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Patel with RenewVest Securities. Please go ahead.

Mike Patel:
What are your expectations for the long-term growth of the renewable energy market?

Sarah Thompson:
Mike, the long-term outlook is tremendous, with BNEF forecasting a $1.7 trillion market through 2030 amid LCOE parity and AI-driven hyperscaler demand—over 12 GW corporate PPAs YTD. We're positioned with 28.5 GW pipeline for 25% EBITDA CAGR, 3.2 GW FY25 CODs, recycling $5-7B into high-IRR greenfield like H2 pilots. Tailwinds include module/BESS deflation, IRA $110B annual capex, REPowerEU; our financing stack, 95% hedges, and hybrids ensure 20%+ EPS CAGR in this net-zero push akin to NextEra/Ørsted scale.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, there appear to be no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back over to Sarah Thompson for any closing remarks.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, everyone, for joining us today. We appreciate your interest in RenewaTech Global. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
